note: Hebrew le'okhlah, "for food"; the produce is grain and fruit, and "meat" (= food in 1611) now means flesh (also v. 7).

Hebrew shofar teru'ah, "a horn of loud blast"; the word "jubilee" (yovel) is first introduced in v. 10, so the KJV's "trumpet of the jubile" anticipates it, and shofar is a ram's horn rather than a metal trumpet.

kjv: if a man purchase of the Levites
mine: whatever is redeemed from the Levites
note: Hebrew wa'asher yig'al min-halewiyim, "and whoever/whatever redeems from the Levites"; the verse is notoriously obscure (the Vulgate inserts "not"), and the KJV takes ga'al loosely as "purchase".

kjv: the field of the suburbs of their (the Levites') cities
mine: the pastureland belonging to their (the Levites') cities
note: Hebrew migrash is the open common land around a town used for grazing; "suburbs" now means residential districts.

kjv: [yea, though he be] a stranger, or a sojourner; that he (your brother) may live with thee
mine: as a foreigner and resident alien he (your brother) shall live with you
note: Hebrew ger wetoshav wachay immakh: the impoverished Israelite brother is to be supported and live alongside you with the status of a resident alien; the KJV's supplied words make the verse extend charity to a foreigner instead.

kjv: Take thou no usury of him (your brother)
note: Hebrew neshekh and tarbit denote any interest or increase on a loan; "usury" now implies only excessive rates (also v. 37).
